origin: council activation #7 (instructions.txt S18), finding 1 — The PhD
hypothesis: train.py's hardcoded lr=3e-4 is tuned for GPT-2-scale width (768-1600) and is far below the optimum for this rig's width (256). A width-appropriate LR reaches a materially lower train loss at equal step count.
why_train_loss_endpoint: Council finding 2 reports the val split is heavily contaminated (val is the tail of the concatenated dpo 'chosen' solutions; data.py splits by character position, not by group). Any val-based endpoint is therefore untrustworthy until that is fixed. Train loss sidesteps it entirely. NOTE: the 68.3% figure is the council's measurement, not independently reproduced by the executor (proprietor ruled out re-verification reads on 2026-07-26).

fixed_config.schedule: cosine with 5% warmup, min_lr = lr/10 (train.py's cosine_lr, unchanged)
fixed_config.optimizer: AdamW betas=(0.9,0.95) wd=0.1, grad clip 1.0 (train.py's, unchanged)

stage_1_sweep.purpose: locate the optimum LR at this width; single seed, NOT the confirmatory test
stage_1_sweep.treatment_selection_rule: the LR with the lowest final train loss becomes the treatment arm. Declared BEFORE running so the choice is mechanical, not eyeballed.

stage_2_confirm.endpoint: final train loss, measured on 40 FIXED eval batches drawn from a dedicated torch.Generator(seed=12345) so every arm and seed sees byte-identical eval batches (this is also council finding 3's fix, applied here first)

success_bar.primary: mean(control train loss) - mean(treatment train loss) >= 0.020
success_bar.secondary: zero overlap between the two arms' 5-seed [min,max] ranges
success_bar.council_basis: PhD's stated bar: >=0.020 mean gap, >3x the measured SE of the difference (0.0060), with zero range overlap

prespecified_outcomes.pass: both bars met -> the shipped lr=3e-4 default is wrong for this width; fix the default and adopt width-scaling (LR ~ 1/width) rather than a new hand-tuned constant.
prespecified_outcomes.fail: gap < 0.020 or ranges overlap -> report as null. Do NOT re-run with different steps/width and report the winner; a second run is a NEW preregistration.
prespecified_outcomes.surprise: if control WINS, report that plainly — it falsifies the council's finding 1 on this rig and that is a result worth having.

not_claimed: That this generalizes to other depths. Council's own leftover risk notes the PhD's table used 2 layers; this runs 4 and does not re-measure the scaling law at each depth.
That train loss is a proxy for model quality. It is the endpoint because val is contaminated, not because it is the better measure.
Any claim about Track A. Untouched by this experiment.
